mcp.off: MCP is disabled — nobody can use it, tokens included.
mcp.safety: Safety rules that cannot be changed: a read-only token never writes; irreversible actions are never on by default; every write is recorded in the audit log; the content editor only lets an assistant create or edit drafts.
mcp.scopeHelp: The ceiling of the token. “Read & write” allows write actions to be granted; you still choose them one by one afterwards.
mcp.toolsHelp: Collected from every active module. Modules and instances can opt out (advanced settings of the instance).
instances.mcp: Offer its actions to the MCP API
instances.mcpHelp: Assistants connected through MCP can use this instance's actions (drafts, internal files…).
mcp.accessIntro: Choose, action by action, what this token may do. Changes apply immediately on the site — no need to create a new token — but your AI assistant only reads its list of tools when it connects: after turning an action on or off, disconnect and reconnect this server in your assistant (or start a new conversation). Each module decides which of its actions are on by default; the others stay off until you turn them on here.
mcp.readCeiling: This is a read-only token: actions that write stay locked, whatever is checked. Create a read & write token to allow them.
mcp.resetAll: Reset every action of this token to the module defaults
mcp.instanceOptedOut: This instance has withdrawn its actions from MCP (advanced settings of the instance): nothing here can be used.
mcp.confirmDestructive: “{action}” is irreversible (it deletes data). Allow this token to do it?
mcp.connect.title: Connect an AI assistant
mcp.connect.intro: Three steps, nothing to install on your site: you create a token, give it to your assistant, and it can then read or prepare drafts according to what you allowed.
mcp.guide.placeholderNote: Replace {marker} with your token. It is only visible when it is created, never here.
mcp.guide.filled: These blocks already contain your token.
mcp.guide.claude.title: Claude (claude.ai and app)
mcp.guide.claude.text: In Claude's settings, under Connectors, add a "custom connector" and paste this secret address. There is nothing else to enter.
mcp.guide.claude.need: It only works if you ticked "Allow connection by secret address" when creating the token.
mcp.guide.secretWarn: This address IS the password: do not share it. It appears in your web server's logs. If it leaks, revoke the token.
mcp.guide.code.title: Claude Code
mcp.guide.code.text: Run this command in a terminal. The token travels in a header, not in the address.
mcp.guide.other.title: Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf and other clients
mcp.guide.other.text: These tools read a small configuration file. The exact field names depend on the client: here are the most common shapes. You always need an address and an Authorization header.
mcp.guide.other.generic: Common format (Claude Code, Cursor, MCP Inspector…): depending on the client, "type" is optional
mcp.guide.test.title: Test the connection
mcp.guide.test.text: Two commands to run in a terminal: the first introduces the client to the site, the second lists the actions this token can use.
mcp.guide.test.expected: Expected reply: JSON text containing "serverInfo" with your site's name, then "tools" with the list of actions. Error 401: token missing or malformed (it must start with vit_). Error 404 on the secret address: option not enabled for this token, or unknown or revoked token. Error 503: MCP is turned off.
mcp.guide.how.title: How it works
mcp.guide.how.token: A token is an assistant's password: it starts with vit_ followed by a long run of letters and digits. Create one per assistant, so you can remove one without touching the others.
mcp.guide.how.header: The token is sent in the header named Authorization, with the word Bearer, a space, then the token: Authorization: Bearer vit_… This is the form standard MCP clients expect.
mcp.guide.how.browser: Opening the address in a browser shows "Use POST": that is normal, assistants do not simply display a page.
mcp.guide.how.rights: Rights are set token by token and action by action: click "Choose actions" next to the token.
mcp.guide.how.transport: Simplified MCP "Streamable HTTP" transport: JSON-RPC 2.0 POST requests, JSON replies, no session or stream; GET and DELETE answer 405 with Allow: POST.
mcp.urlOptionHelp: For Claude (claude.ai), which can only take an address. The address IS the password: do not share it; it appears in your web server's logs; revoke the token if it leaks. It is shown only once, at creation.
mcp.created.once: Copy them now: the site only keeps a fingerprint of the token and can never show it again. For a new address, create another token.
mcp.url.title: Connection by secret address
mcp.url.help: For assistants, like Claude (claude.ai), that can only take an address: {siteUrl}/api/mcp/ followed by the token. The full address is shown only when the token is created, the site cannot display it again: for a new one, create another token.

modules.error.uptodate: This module is already up to date.
modules.error.pinned: This module is pinned to a specific commit: it does not update.
migration.failed: Updating this instance's data failed: it was put back to its previous state and set aside (it does not run on half-converted data). A copy of the database is in data/backups/. Fix or update the module, then retry.
migration.newer: This instance's data is newer than the installed module's code (backup restored into an older module?). Update the module, then retry.
migration.floor: This instance's data is too far behind this version of the module (data at version {from}, at least version {floor} is needed). Nothing was changed. First install an in-between version of this module (ask its author which one), then update it and retry.

legacy.title: Maintenance
legacy.intro: What is left to upgrade after a Curiosa update. You can run the upgrade again here, and decide what to do with modules that are no longer offered.
legacy.pending: The data upgrade is not finished yet. Your public site works normally. It resumes by itself at every start; you can also run it again below.
legacy.clean: Nothing to report: everything is up to date.
legacy.report.help: Numbers and names only: no setting value is ever shown here.
legacy.row.sourceRows: Extensions to move to the catalogue
legacy.row.sourceRows.help: These extensions work, but they come from a copy made by an earlier version of Curiosa. Update them: they will move to the catalogue without losing any data.
legacy.row.switchedOff.help: The "switched off" state no longer exists. At the next start, these items will be uninstalled and their data kept.
legacy.row.behind: Instances whose data waits for an upgrade
legacy.row.behind.help: They will be upgraded at the next start, or right away with "Run again".
legacy.row.failed.help: Their upgrade did not succeed. Open each one to see why, then "Retry".
legacy.row.newer.help: Their data comes from a newer version of the extension (restored backup?). Update the extension.
legacy.row.seedsMissing.help: These instances must hand an address or a setting to another extension. This happens at their next update.
legacy.row.collections.help: The extension empties it itself once the transfer is confirmed. It stays in your backups.
legacy.row.legacyValues.help: The extension uses them for a transfer and erases them once it is done. They are never shown.
legacy.row.orphans.help: Their extension no longer declares these settings. They are kept, have no effect, and need nothing from you.
legacy.rerun.help: Runs the start-up upgrade again (20 seconds at most, no Internet). Safe: what is already done is not redone.
legacy.rerun.pending: Some items are left: see the list above.
legacy.rerun.timeout: Time ran out before the end. Run it again in a few minutes: it resumes where it stopped.
legacy.rerun.busy: An upgrade is already running. Try again in a minute.
legacy.banner.title: Data upgrade not finished
legacy.banner.text: Your public site works normally. Part of the data still needs an upgrade.
legacy.banner.owner: The site owner can see what is left in Maintenance.
legacy.result.kept: Noted: this module stays as it is and no longer holds back the upgrade.
legacy.result.removed: Module removed. Its data is kept: if you install it again, you will get it back.
legacy.result.erased: Module removed, and its data erased.
legacy.result.refused: Nothing was changed: this module is no longer in this list, or could not be removed.
legacy.again: The upgrade had finished, but some items are left again (an older backup may have been restored). See the list below.
legacy.almost: Everything is in order. It only needs to be noticed: press "Run the upgrade again" below.
legacy.absent.title: Modules that are no longer offered
legacy.absent.help: The catalogue no longer offers these modules, so they cannot update by themselves. They still work; the choice is yours.
legacy.absent.choose: What do you want to do? Pick an equivalent module in Extensions and then remove this one, or remove it without losing anything (its data is kept), or keep it as it is.
legacy.absent.keepConfirm: Keep "{name}" as it is? It keeps working, but will not be updated. It will no longer hold back the upgrade.
legacy.absent.keepHelp: Nothing changes on your site. You can change your mind later.
legacy.kept.title: Modules kept as they are
legacy.kept.help: You chose to keep them. They do not hold back the upgrade.
legacy.kept.undo: Stop keeping it as it is

settings.glow.tuningHelp: Used when "Custom" is chosen above. Out-of-range values are brought back to the nearest limit.
settings.glow.sizeHelp: 30 to 120. A large spot blends into the background.

settings.glow.hueHelp: 0: all in the accent colour. 180: each spot may take any hue around the accent (±°).
settings.glow.intensityHelp: Maximum opacity of a spot's core, 5 to 50.
settings.glow.seedHelp: 1 to 9999. Changes the random positions, sizes and hues; the same value always gives the same layout.
settings.bgHelp: A backdrop behind the content, built from your colours. It adds to the glow above.
settings.bgCustomHelp: Used when "Custom" is chosen. A list of layers (gradient, spots, dots, grid, image), 6 at most: see docs/BACKGROUND.md. Nothing is saved if the description is invalid.
navigation.empty: Your menu is empty for now. Add a page of your site or a link.
navigation.pickPage: Which page do you want in the menu?
settings.glow.colorHelp: Used when the box above is unchecked. The "hue shift" applies starting from this colour.
settings.bgSvgHelp: Paste the code of an SVG drawing (exported from Inkscape, Figma, Illustrator…): gradients, dot patterns, silhouettes, motifs. It needs a viewBox. Colours can follow the theme: write {accent}, {bg}, {fg}… instead of a colour code. No scripts, text or embedded images: see docs/BACKGROUND.md.
settings.bgSvgAlignHelp: When the window doesn't have the drawing's proportions, the drawing is cropped: choose which side stays visible.
settings.faviconHelp: A square image (png, jpg, webp or gif; 64 × 64 px or larger). Without an image, the site builds an icon from its colours.
instances.sortHelp: Newest first by default. A "featured" entry always comes first.
sort.title: By title (A → Z)
settings.statsHelp: Daily counters shown on the dashboard: no IP address, cookie or identifier is ever kept. Visitors who refuse tracking (Do Not Track) are not counted.
dashboard.visitsPrivacy: Anonymous counting: no personal data is kept.
redirects.examples: Examples: /twitch → your channel, /shop → your online shop, /donate → your support page.
settings.logosHelp: Upload what you have: nothing is required, the site does its best with the images it receives.
settings.logoWideHelp: Symbol and name side by side. Shown at the top of the site instead of the written name.
settings.logoSquareHelp: The symbol alone. Used small (phone, badges) and in place of the horizontal logo when it is missing.
settings.logoShareHelp: Shown when the site is shared (social networks, messengers). Ideal: 1200 × 630 px. Without one, the site uses your icon.
settings.logosDarkHelp: If your site has a dark background and your logo is dark, upload a light version here. The site picks the right one from the background color.
navigation.groupEmpty: This submenu is empty: on the item right below it, use "Put in …" to fill it. An empty submenu is not saved.
settings.headerHelp: Choose the layout of the top of your pages. The logo, menu, languages and the elements below place themselves.
settings.header.classicHelp: Logo on the left, menu on the right.
settings.header.twoRowsHelp: Logo and button on top, menu below.
settings.header.centeredHelp: Logo in the middle, menu centered below.
settings.header.minimalHelp: Logo and a "Menu" button: discreet, on large screens too.
settings.header.socials: Show my social networks in the header

settings.header.socialsHelp.one: Active network: {count}. Each network is a module: add or remove it from Modules.
settings.header.socialsNone: No social network yet. Each network (Twitch, YouTube…) is a module: add one from Modules and its icon appears here by itself.
settings.header.label: Text
settings.header.linksHelp: A link or button only appears when both its text and address are filled. The address is a site page (/contact), an https://… link or mailto:…
settings.privacyHelp: What the site measures, what it leaves to robots, and its privacy page. Unless a visitor turns on the “news” button, no tracking cookie is set (only the chosen-language one).
settings.newsToggle: Show a cookie banner (news since the last visit)
settings.newsToggleHelp: Shows a banner at the bottom of the screen explaining what the site's cookies are for (the language, and with the visitor's consent the date of their last visit to flag news), with "Accept cookies" and "No thanks". Nothing is stored until the visitor accepts, and a "Cookies" link in the footer lets them withdraw consent. Off: no banner, no link, and no news dots in the menu.
privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: This page describes what the site "{name}" records about you. It is generated automatically from how the site really works.
privacy.whoContact: The site "{name}" is run by its owner. For any question about your data, write to {email}.
privacy.whoNoContact: The site "{name}" is run by its owner. For any question about your data, use the contact details given on the site.
privacy.cookies: Cookies and storage in your browser
privacy.cookies.locale: **Language**: the site remembers the language you choose (cookie "curiosa_locale", 1 year). It is needed to show you the site in the right language.
privacy.cookies.news: **News**: only if you click "Accept cookies" in the site's banner, the site remembers in your browser the date of your last visit to flag what is new since you last came (cookies "curiosa_news", "curiosa_seen" and "curiosa_since", up to 1 year). Nothing is sent anywhere else. You can withdraw your consent at any time with the "Cookies" link in the footer: everything is then erased.
privacy.cookies.choice: **Your answer**: if you answer "No thanks" to the cookie banner, the site remembers that refusal (cookie "curiosa_cookies", 30 days) so it does not ask again on every page. If you close the banner with the Escape key, that marker only lasts for your visit. It only holds a plain "no" or "later".
privacy.cookies.none: The site sets no advertising or tracking cookie and uses no third-party measurement service.
privacy.stats.on: The site counts its visits anonymously: page views, most read pages and where visitors come from, as daily counters. Nothing is stored in your browser and your IP address is never recorded; to count a visitor only once a day, the server derives a single-use fingerprint from it, deleted the next day, which cannot recognise you from one day to the next. Visitors who send "Do Not Track" or "Global Privacy Control" are not counted.
privacy.stats.off: The site does not count its visits.
privacy.features: Data collected by the site's features
privacy.rights.text: You can ask for access to the data about you, for its correction or erasure, object to its processing, or lodge a complaint with the competent data protection authority.
settings.privacyPageHelp: The mandatory text (cookies, statistics, data of your features, visitors' rights) is generated from what the site really does: it shows at the bottom of every page and cannot be removed. You can only add your own information to it.
settings.privacyExtraHelp: Simple Markdown. Shown after the mandatory text: data controller, retention period, how to exercise rights…
home.core.media.help: A title, a paragraph, a button, with one or more images beside it.
home.core.tabs.help: A list of tabs: visitors click a name to read its text (benefits, plans, steps…).
home.core.stats.help: A few big numbers with a caption (members, events, years…).
home.core.cta.help: A title, a sentence and a prominent button to invite people to sign up, write or discover.
home.core.video.help: A big title set over a video playing in the background (uploaded to your site).
block.kindHelp.media: Text on one side, images on the other. Perfect to present your activity or a novelty. Everything is optional: fill in only what you want to show.
block.kindHelp.tabs: Tabs: each has a name, a heading and a text. Visitors click to switch. Add one tab per benefit, plan or step.

block.kindHelp.cta: A short message with a button, to prompt an action: sign up, write to you, discover a page.
block.kindHelp.video: Your text appears over a video playing in the background, only while it is on screen. Upload a short, light video (MP4 or WebM).
block.title: Title

block.imagesTabsHelp: Up to three images shared by all tabs; a tab can have its own image, which replaces them.
block.videoHelp: MP4 or WebM, 50 MB at most. Prefer a short, light video that loops.
block.sound: Let visitors turn the sound on

block.bgHelp: Placed behind the content. Tip: an image sized like the block, prepared with your own elements, lets you put a visual exactly where you want.

catalogue.sources.removeConfirm: Remove this repository from the list? Modules already installed stay installed.
catalogue.sources.none: No module found in this repository.
modules.error.sourceSubdir: Give the repository address without a folder: its modules are found automatically.

setup.modules.help: A module adds a feature to your site (a blog, your social networks, pages…). Here are the ones we suggest to get started.
setup.modules.skip: You can skip this step without any risk: nothing is required, and every module (these and many more) can be added or removed later from the admin, under Features → Add.
setup.modules.none: No module to suggest for now: you can add some from the admin whenever you like.
setup.modules.unreachable: The catalogue cannot be reached right now, so no module is suggested. No problem: your site is still created, and you can install modules later from Modules › Catalogue.

account.sessionsHelp: You are signed in on this device, and maybe on others. If you lost a phone or lent your computer, you can sign out every device at once, this one included.
account.sessionsConfirm: Sign out all your devices, including this one?
users.revokeConfirm: Sign this person out of all their devices? They can sign back in with their password.
login.changed: Password changed: sign in again with the new one.
login.codeHelp: Open the authenticator app on your phone and enter the 6-digit code shown. No phone? Enter one of your backup codes.
account.twofa.title: Two-step verification
account.twofa.help: After your password, you are asked for a 6-digit code that changes every 30 seconds, shown by an app on your phone (Google Authenticator, Authy, 1Password…). Even if someone found your password, they could not get in.
account.twofa.scan: 1. In your authenticator app, add an account by scanning this code, or by typing the key below.
account.twofa.confirm: 2. Enter the 6-digit code shown by the app to confirm
account.twofa.codesHelp: Write them down or print them, and keep them somewhere safe (password manager, paper). If you lose your phone, each one lets you in once. They will never be shown again.
account.twofa.codesDone: Got it, I kept my codes
account.twofa.disableHelp: To turn off, confirm with your password and a code from the app (or a backup code). You will be signed out.
account.twofa.regenHelp: New codes replace all the old ones. Confirm with your password.
account.twofa.required: The site owner requires two-step verification: you cannot turn it off.
account.twofa.need: The site owner requires two-step verification for the whole team: turn it on to continue.
users.twofaReset: Reset their two-step verification and passkeys
users.twofaResetConfirm: Remove this person's two-step verification and passkeys (they also lose their open sessions)? They can set them up again from My account.
users.require2fa: Require two-step verification for the whole team
users.require2faHelp: Everyone will have to turn it on at their next visit. You must have turned it on yourself first.
users.require2faNeedsYou: First turn on two-step verification on your own account (My account).

account.passkeys.help: Sign in with your device's fingerprint, face or code (or a security key), with no password or code. It is the safest method: a fake site cannot steal it. Register one per device.
account.passkeys.name: Name (e.g. My phone)
account.passkeys.removeHelp: Remove this passkey? Confirm with your password.
account.passkeys.unsupported: This browser does not support passkeys.
account.passkeys.failed: The passkey could not be registered.
account.passkeys.max: You reached the maximum number of passkeys (10).

instances.error.groupRequired: To save "{group}", fill in: {fields} (or remove it).

home.noFeatures: The features you install (blog, calendar…) will also be available here.
entries.emptyHelp: Write your first entry: it stays a draft, invisible on the site, until you publish it.
entries.sharedHint: The image, link, code and dates are the same for every language.
entries.status.draftHelp: Only visible here. Nothing appears on the site: take your time.
entries.status.publishedHelp: Visible to everyone on the site.
entries.summaryHelp: One or two sentences shown on cards and in previews. Empty = the beginning of the content.

entries.newIntro: Start with the title. The entry is saved as a draft until you choose “Published”.
entries.created: Entry created. You can keep editing it here.
entries.dangerHelp: Deleting is permanent. To simply take it off the site, choose “Draft” above instead.

entries.deleteConfirm: Permanently delete “{title}”? This cannot be undone.
entries.deleteVersionConfirm: Delete this language version? The other languages are untouched. This cannot be undone.
sources.allUsed: Every source is used, including ones you add later.
sources.onlyChecked: Only the checked sources are used.
aim.notice.busy: Another maintenance operation is running. The request stays pending: try again in a minute.
aim.notice.expired: This request has expired: it will not be run. The AI can ask again.
aim.notice.not-pending: This request has already been answered.
aim.notice.forbidden: Only the site owner can answer a request.
aim.pending.title: Requests waiting for your approval
aim.pending.help: Your AI does nothing risky without you. Read what is going to happen, then approve or refuse. A request left unanswered expires after 24 hours and never runs.
aim.pending.none: No request is waiting. When your AI wants to do something risky, you will see it here before anything is done.
aim.denyConfirm: Refuse this request? It will never be run.
aim.req.core_update: Update Curiosa from version {from} to version {to}.
aim.req.module_update: Update the feature "{name}" from version {from} to version {to}.
aim.req.module_uninstall: Uninstall the feature "{name}", keeping its data aside (it comes back if the feature is installed again).

aim.risk.module_update: This feature's data is kept. If something goes wrong, the old version is put back.
aim.risk.modules_update_all: They are updated one at a time; one that fails does not stop the others. Data is kept.
aim.risk.module_uninstall: Permanent: the feature, its settings and all its data disappear. Only a backup can bring them back.
aim.action.backup_run: make a safety copy of the database

aim.notify.email: In the admin and by email
aim.notify.emailHelp: An email goes to the site owner when a request is waiting and when an AI took an action. It contains no password or secret. Email sending must be set up in the site settings.
aim.notify.mailMissing: Email sending is not set up yet: until it is, you will only get the notices in the admin.

aim.approval.direct: The AI acts without asking me
aim.approval.directHelp: Careful: updates and uninstalls happen right away, without your approval. Keep this for an AI you fully trust.
aim.approval.directConfirm: Let "{token}" update and uninstall without your approval? You will only be told afterwards.
aim.guideHelp: A text to give your AI: what it may do, in which order, and when to ask you.

aim.tool.modules: List of installed features, the ones in error, what they lack, the ones with an update.
aim.tool.updates: Updates available for Curiosa (stable versions only) and for features.
aim.tool.diagnose: A simple report: what is wrong, the probable cause and what to do.

aim.tool.module_uninstall: Uninstall a feature with all its data (permanent).
